Plant is too young to see how petals curve over fruits, but none of the photos of reflexed petal group shows any hairiness on the sepals, so selected "Petals curving over fruit in age", 
"Petals > sepals", 
"filaments 5-6 mm" measured at 6mm, 
"sepals densely hairy" yes, so keys to Limnanthes alba subsp. alba

description:
In my yard in residential Chicago

At least two seedlings adjacent to the clump of swamp saxifrage, towards the upper right quadrant. I initially seeded this species into my garden 3 springs ago. This is the second spring where plants popped up spontaneously through reseeding. But these are the only two Floerkea plants I've found this year. It's curious that they have grown directly on a transplanted clump of swamp saxifrage that came from the same garden where the Floerkea seed was sourced. I wonder if the soil microbiome in this clump might have promoted seed germination. I have numerous clumps of plants obtained from northern Wisconsin in areas with healthy remnant microbial communities, yet I haven't found any Floerkea on those clumps in the past. Perhaps Floerkea requires or prefers microbes and conditions that aren't present in the Wisconsin soil?
